brief:
## Decided so far
- Project goal: design an original, trendy, user-friendly TV-only remote (not a multi-remote) via a three-phase design process, priced to sell at 25 Euros with production cost around 12.5 Euros. [TS3012a: "our new project is about we need design a remote control for television set, so, which has to be original, trendy and user-friendly."] [TS3012a: "Selling price, twenty five Euros."]
- Design must stay intuitive (familiar controls, no radical redesign) and accessible to disabled users. [TS3012a: "thing to keep in mind is that we need to stick to what people are familiar with. No rational changes or whatever, 'cause it revolutionary changes, yes."] [TS3012a: "Do we want people who are disabled in any way to uh, yeah, to be able to use it as well?"]
- Target market is young, fashion-conscious users aged roughly 16-40, since 75% of people find current remotes ugly. [TS3012b: "we want to appeal to younger people, which are um the younger people were defined under forty."] [TS3012b: "seventy five percent of the users find most remote controls ugly."]
- Fewer, larger, more durable buttons; power, channel and volume are the essential core buttons, and mute is deprioritized. [TS3012b: "So what we want to go to is not this one, but more less buttons, easy, some bigger buttons."] [TS3012b: "It's not that important, no."]
- Layout: power button on top, channel/volume grouped top-right, square menu button in the middle, and a favorite-channel button as one of four extra top buttons. [TS3012b: "I think the bu the power button should be on top, 'cause it's the first thing you do, turn it on."] [TS3012c: "One of the four. Uh, it's better than, I think."]
- Remote is universal across TV brands and shaped distinctively from competitors (rounded edges, curved banana-shaped back for grip) rather than copying designs like Sony's. [TS3012b: "I think it's universal. I think we should go for universal, because apparently we're a separate company making separate c remote controls"] [TS3012c: "Then it will bounce and you don't drop it so easily."]
- Case material is rubber (spongy, drop-protective) in yellow with black buttons; interchangeable covers (e.g. fruit/vegetable shapes) let the base design stay stable while covers follow trends. [TS3012c: "I think the spongy feel gives us rubber."] [TS3012c: "I think we should th then take it take yellow. Take what you c yellow remote control."]
- Two editions planned: deluxe with LCD screen on top and advanced chip (number keys at bottom), and standard without LCD (keys at top); LCD justified by strong target-group demand. [TS3012c: "I have two designs, one including uh an L_C_D_ screen, wh which is basically the deluxe edition. And then I also have a standard edition"] [TS3012c: "let's say because it is uh very hot in n our target group I think, we should take it take it t to consideration to build an L_C_D_ screen in it."]
- Voice recognition will be implemented via a newly found small, standards-compliant component, since 60-70% of target users want it; microphone placed on top. [TS3012c: "If it's small, if it's fits, if if people like it, why not?"] [TS3012c: "I think on top."]
- Interface uses push-buttons, not a scroll wheel (dropped as non-functional); power comes from regular batteries (not kinetic/solar), not a rechargeable system. [TS3012c: "If we don't need it, why put it in your why put it in your in your if it's if it's not something people are looking for or is useful."] [TS3012c: "Uh energy, we choose regular regular batteries."]

## What changed along the way
- LCD screen: originally dropped in meeting 2 for draining batteries and being too costly, then reinstated in meeting 3 for the deluxe edition due to strong target-group demand. [TS3012b: "I think we should lose the L_C_D_ screen, like you said. I think for example it's it's huge I think the L_C_D_ is huge, it consumes batteries like hell."] [TS3012c: "let's say because it is uh very hot in n our target group I think, we should take it take it t to consideration to build an L_C_D_ screen in it."]
- Speech recognition: originally dropped in meeting 2 as too hard to implement across multiple language markets, then reinstated in meeting 3 after a small, standards-compliant component was found. [TS3012b: "Speech recognition, I think it's very hard, because we're selling across multiple countries. So I think implementing speech recognition is such a small um apparatus, it's very hard to do."] [TS3012c: "If it's small, if it's fits, if if people like it, why not?"]
- Power source: meeting 2 tasked investigating a rechargeable docking-battery system, but meeting 3 instead chose plain regular batteries for being common and familiar to users. [TS3012b: "I'm going to try to find that out. I'm not sure if there's information available on this, but"] [TS3012c: "Why not? I mean everybody everybody knows how to use that. It's it's common. So and it's available everywhere."]

## Open actions and owners
- Conduct trend-watching research on what younger users want to finalize cover/design decisions. Owner: Speaker D (marketing). [TS3012b: "I want some you should do some trend-watching, because even if we're if we're gonna do those covers and everything, what people really want"]
- Confirm whether customers are willing to pay extra for a rechargeable feature beyond the 25 Euro base price. Owner: Speaker A (project manager). [TS3012b: "or maybe you can find out i what people are willing to pay."]
- Research whether modern TVs already expose brightness and other advanced functions via an on-screen menu. Owner: Speaker C (industrial designer). [TS3012b: "Uh isn't there a possibility to do research on that, so we know that for sure?"]
- Brainstorm a branded product name instead of using a vague serial number. Owner: Speaker C (industrial designer), for the whole team. [TS3012b: "Shall we all try uh to think about a name?"]
- Finish the market analysis and the year-end project report before the final meeting. Owner: Speaker C (industrial designer) for market analysis, Speaker A (project manager) for the report. [TS3012c: "I'm supposed to do the little work on the year-end report. So the project report."]
- Prepare and bring the final polished design sketch to the last meeting. Owner: Speaker B (user interface designer). [TS3012c: "You doodle a doodle us a nice nice design for for the next meeting, we'll be done."]

## Disagreements still open
- Whether interchangeable covers should include swappable button sleeves (Nokia-style) or only the outer casing is still unresolved. [TS3012b: "Either either change both the buttons and and the cover or just the cover, I'm not sure which which is easier"]
